names: Mother of Liu Qing of Liu'an

units.zh: 孝景皇帝子凡十三人為王，而母五人，同母者為宗親。
units.en: Emperor Jing had thirteen sons who were enfeoffed as kings, each born to one of five mothers. Those who shared the same mother were reckoned as one maternal lineage.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaojing had thirteen sons who became kings, born to five different mothers. Those from the same mother were considered clan relatives.

units.zh: 栗姬子曰榮、德、閼于。
units.en: Consort Li bore three sons: Rong, De, and Eyu.
units.literal: Consort Li's sons were Rong, De, and A Yu.

units.zh: 程姬子曰餘、非、端。
units.en: Consort Cheng bore three sons: Yu, Fei, and Duan.
units.literal: Consort Cheng's sons were Yu, Fei, and Duan.

units.zh: 賈夫人子曰彭祖、勝。
units.en: Lady Jia bore two sons: Pengzu and Sheng.
units.literal: Lady Jia's sons were Pengzu and Sheng.

units.zh: 唐姬子曰發。
units.en: Consort Tang bore one son: Fa.
units.literal: Consort Tang's son was Fa.

units.zh: 王夫人兒姁子曰越、寄、乘、舜。
units.en: Lady Wang, also known as Erxu, bore four sons: Yue, Ji, Cheng, and Shun.
units.literal: Lady Wang, Erxu, bore sons Yue, Ji, Cheng, and Shun.

units.zh: 河閒獻王德，以孝景帝前二年用皇子為河閒王。
units.en: King Xian of Hejian, whose name was De, was enfeoffed as King of Hejian as an imperial prince in the second year of Emperor Jing's early reign.
units.literal: King Xian of Hejian, De, was made King of Hejian as imperial son in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's early reign.

units.zh: 好儒學，被服造次必於儒者。
units.en: He was devoted to Confucian learning, and in both his dress and his conduct, even in moments of haste, he invariably adhered to the ways of the Confucian scholars.
units.literal: He loved Confucian learning. Even in his clothing and hasty actions, he always followed Confucian scholars.

units.zh: 山東諸儒多從之游。
units.en: Many Confucian scholars from east of the mountains came to study under him.
units.literal: Many Confucian scholars from Shandong traveled to study with him.

units.zh: 二十六年卒，子共王不害立。
units.en: After twenty-six years on the throne he died, and his son, King Gong, whose name was Buhai, succeeded him.
units.literal: He died after twenty-six years. His son, King Gong Bu Hai, succeeded him.

units.zh: 四年卒，子剛王基代立。
units.en: He died after four years, and his son, King Gang, whose name was Ji, took the throne.
units.literal: He died after four years. His son, King Gang Ji, succeeded him.

units.zh: 十二年卒，子頃王授代立。
units.en: He died after twelve years, and his son, King Qing, whose name was Shou, succeeded him.
units.literal: He died after twelve years. His son, King Qing Shou, succeeded him.

units.zh: 臨江哀王閼于，以孝景帝前二年用皇子為臨江王。
units.en: King Ai of Linjiang, whose name was Eyu, was enfeoffed as King of Linjiang as an imperial prince in the second year of Emperor Jing's early reign.
units.literal: King Ai of Linjiang, Eyu, was made King of Linjiang as imperial son in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's early reign.

units.zh: 三年卒，無後，國除為郡。
units.en: He died after three years without an heir, and his kingdom was abolished and converted into a commandery.
units.literal: He died after three years without heirs. The kingdom was abolished as a commandery.

units.zh: 臨江閔王榮，以孝景前四年為皇太子，四歲廢，用故太子為臨江王。
units.en: King Min of Linjiang, whose name was Rong, was made Crown Prince in the fourth year of Emperor Jing's early reign. After four years he was deposed, and the former Crown Prince was then enfeoffed as King of Linjiang.
units.literal: King Min of Linjiang, Rong, was made crown prince in the fourth year of Emperor Xiaojing's early reign. He was deposed after four years and the former crown prince was made King of Linjiang.

units.zh: 四年，坐侵廟壖垣為宮，上徵榮。
units.en: In his fourth year as king, he was charged with encroaching upon the temple precinct walls to expand his palace. The emperor summoned Rong to the capital.
units.literal: In his fourth year, he was convicted of encroaching on the temple grounds to build a palace. The emperor summoned Rong to court.

units.zh: 榮行，祖於江陵北門。
units.en: As Rong departed, he performed the farewell sacrifice at the north gate of Jiangling.
units.literal: As Rong departed, he performed farewell rites at Jiangling's north gate.

units.zh: 既已上車，軸折車廢。
units.en: He had already mounted his carriage when the axle snapped and the carriage collapsed.
units.literal: He had already boarded his carriage when the axle broke and the carriage was ruined.

units.zh: 江陵父老流涕竊言曰：「吾王不反矣！」
units.en: The elders of Jiangling wept and whispered to one another, "Our king will never return!"
units.literal: The elders of Jiangling wept and whispered among themselves: 'Our king will never return!'

units.zh: 榮至，詣中尉府簿。
units.en: When Rong arrived in the capital, he presented himself at the office of the Commandant of Justice to be registered.
units.literal: When Rong arrived, he reported to the Commandant of Justice's office.

units.zh: 中尉郅都責訊王，王恐，自殺。
units.en: The Commandant Zhi Du interrogated the king with harsh rebukes; terrified, Rong took his own life.
units.literal: Commandant Zhi Du interrogated the king, who became terrified and committed suicide.

units.zh: 葬藍田。
units.en: He was buried at Lantian.
units.literal: He was buried at Lantian.

units.zh: 燕數萬銜土置冢上，百姓憐之。
units.en: Tens of thousands of swallows carried earth in their beaks and placed it upon his tomb, and the common people mourned him.
units.literal: Tens of thousands of swallows carried earth in their beaks and placed it on his tomb mound. The common people pitied him.

units.zh: 榮最長，死無後，國除，地入于漢，為南郡。
units.en: Rong had been the eldest son, but he died without an heir. His kingdom was abolished, and its territory was absorbed into the Han domain as Nan Commandery.
units.literal: Rong was the eldest but died without heirs. The kingdom was abolished and its territory incorporated into Han as Nan Commandery.

units.zh: 右三國本王皆栗姬之子也。
units.en: The original kings of these three states were all sons of Consort Li.
units.literal: These three kingdoms were originally ruled by sons of Consort Li.

units.zh: 魯共王餘，以孝景前二年用皇子為淮陽王。
units.en: King Gong of Lu, whose name was Yu, was first enfeoffed as King of Huaiyang as an imperial prince in the second year of Emperor Jing's early reign.
units.literal: King Gong of Lu, Yu, was made King of Huaiyang as imperial son in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's early reign.

units.zh: 二年，吳楚反破後，以孝景前三年徙為魯王。
units.en: Two years later, after the rebellion of Wu and Chu had been crushed, he was transferred to become King of Lu in the third year of Emperor Jing's early reign.
units.literal: In the second year, after the Wu and Chu rebellion was crushed, he was moved to become King of Lu in the third year of Emperor Xiaojing's early reign.

units.zh: 好治宮室苑囿狗馬。
units.en: He delighted in building palaces and gardens, and in keeping dogs and horses.
units.literal: He enjoyed constructing palaces, gardens, and parks, as well as dogs and horses.

units.zh: 季年好音，不喜辭辯。
units.en: In his later years he grew fond of music but had no taste for literary disputation.
units.literal: In his later years he loved music but disliked literary debate.

units.zh: 為人吃。
units.en: He had a stammer.
units.literal: In disposition he stammered.

units.zh: 二十六年卒，子光代為王。
units.en: After twenty-six years on the throne he died, and his son Guang succeeded him as king.
units.literal: He died after twenty-six years. His son Guang succeeded to the throne.

units.zh: 初好音輿馬；
units.en: In his early years he was fond of music, carriages, and horses;
units.literal: At first he loved music and chariots.

units.zh: 晚節嗇，惟恐不足於財。
units.en: but in his later years he grew parsimonious, ever fearful that his wealth might prove insufficient.
units.literal: In his later years he became miserly, always fearing he lacked sufficient wealth.

units.zh: 江都易王非，以孝景前二年用皇子為汝南王。
units.en: King Yi of Jiangdu, whose name was Fei, was enfeoffed as King of Runan as an imperial prince in the second year of Emperor Jing's early reign.
units.literal: King Yi of Jiangdu, Fei, was made King of Runan as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's second year before his reign.

units.zh: 吳楚反時，非年十五，有材力，上書願擊吳。
units.en: When the kingdoms of Wu and Chu rose in rebellion, Fei was only fifteen, yet he possessed both talent and strength, and he submitted a memorial requesting permission to march against Wu.
units.literal: During the Wu and Chu rebellion, Fei was fifteen and possessed talent and strength. He submitted a memorial volunteering to attack Wu.

units.zh: 景帝賜非將軍印，擊吳。
units.en: Emperor Jing bestowed upon Fei a general's seal and dispatched him to fight against Wu.
units.literal: Emperor Jing granted Fei a general's seal and sent him to attack Wu.

units.zh: 吳已破，二歲，徙為江都王，治吳故國，以軍功賜天子旌旗。
units.en: After Wu was crushed, two years passed before Fei was transferred to become King of Jiangdu, governing the former territory of Wu. In recognition of his military valor, he was awarded the imperial banners.
units.literal: After Wu was defeated, two years later he was moved to become King of Jiangdu, ruling the former Wu territory. For his military achievements, he was granted the emperor's banners.

units.zh: 元光五年，匈奴大入漢為賊，非上書願擊匈奴，上不許。
units.en: In the fifth year of the Yuanguang era, the Xiongnu launched a major incursion into Han territory, raiding and plundering. Fei submitted a memorial requesting permission to strike against them, but the emperor refused.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanguang, the Xiongnu invaded Han territory on a large scale. Fei petitioned to attack the Xiongnu, but the emperor would not allow it.

units.zh: 非好氣力，治宮觀，招四方豪桀，驕奢甚。
units.en: Fei delighted in feats of strength, built lavish palaces and towers, and gathered bold and daring men from every quarter. His arrogance and extravagance knew no bounds.
units.literal: Fei was fond of physical strength and built palaces and towers. He attracted bold heroes from all directions and lived in great extravagance.

units.zh: 立二十六年卒，子建立為王。
units.en: After twenty-six years on the throne he died, and his son Jian was established as king in his stead.
units.literal: He reigned for twenty-six years and died. His son Jian succeeded him.

units.zh: 七年自殺。
units.en: Seven years later, Jian took his own life.
units.literal: He committed suicide after seven years.

units.zh: 淮南、衡山謀反時，建頗聞其謀。
units.en: When the kings of Huainan and Hengshan were plotting rebellion, Jian had caught wind of their conspiracy.
units.literal: During the Huainan and Hengshan rebellion, Jian had heard rumors of their plot.

units.zh: 自以為國近淮南，恐一日發，為所并，即陰作兵器，而時佩其父所賜將軍印，載天子旗以出。
units.en: Believing his kingdom lay dangerously close to Huainan, he feared that should the revolt erupt, he might be swallowed up. He therefore had weapons forged in secret, and whenever he ventured out he wore the general's seal his father had received and displayed the imperial banners.
units.literal: Since his kingdom bordered Huainan, he feared that if rebellion broke out he would be annexed. So he secretly manufactured weapons while always wearing his father's general's seal and going out with the emperor's banners.

units.zh: 易王死未葬，建有所說易王寵美人淖姬，夜使人迎與姦服舍中。
units.en: Before King Yi had even been laid to rest, Jian became enamored of the late king's favored consort, Lady Nao. Under cover of night he sent men to bring her to his quarters, where he took her as his own.
units.literal: Before King Yi was even buried, Jian took a fancy to King Yi's favored beauty Nao Ji and sent men at night to bring her to his chambers for illicit relations.

units.zh: 及淮南事發，治黨與頗及江都王建。
units.en: When the Huainan conspiracy was uncovered, the investigation of its accomplices extended to implicate King Jian of Jiangdu.
units.literal: When the Huainan affair broke out, the investigation of accomplices implicated King Jian of Jiangdu.

units.zh: 建恐，因使人多持金錢，事絕其獄。
units.en: Jian grew alarmed and dispatched agents laden with gold and coin to bribe officials and quash the proceedings against him.
units.literal: Jian became frightened and sent men with large amounts of gold and money to bribe officials and suppress the case.

units.zh: 而又信巫祝，使人禱祠妄言。
units.en: He also relied on shamans and diviners, sending them to offer prayers and utter slanderous prophecies.
units.literal: He also trusted shamans and prayer-officiants, sending them to perform sacrifices and spread false claims.

units.zh: 建又盡與其姊弟姦。
units.en: Jian further committed incest with all of his elder sisters and younger brothers.
units.literal: Jian also committed incest with all his elder sisters and younger brothers.

units.zh: 事既聞，漢公卿請捕治建。
units.en: When these affairs came to light, the ministers and nobles of the Han court petitioned for Jian's arrest and prosecution.
units.literal: When this became known, Han nobles requested Jian's arrest and trial.

units.zh: 天子不忍，使大臣即訊王。
units.en: The Son of Heaven could not bear to act so harshly and instead sent senior ministers to interrogate the king in person.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven spared him and sent ministers to interrogate the king.

units.zh: 王服所犯，遂自殺。
units.en: The king confessed to his offenses and then took his own life.
units.literal: The king admitted his crimes and committed suicide.

units.zh: 國除，地入于漢，為廣陵郡。
units.en: His kingdom was abolished, its territory absorbed into the Han domain and reorganized as the Commandery of Guangling.
units.literal: The kingdom was abolished and its territory incorporated into Han as Guangling Commandery.

units.zh: 膠西于王端，以孝景前三年吳楚七國反破後，端用皇子為膠西王。
units.en: King Yu of Jiaoxi, whose name was Duan, was enfeoffed as King of Jiaoxi as an imperial prince in the third year of Emperor Jing's early reign, after the rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms of Wu and Chu had been put down.
units.literal: King Yu of Jiaoxi, Duan, was made King of Jiaoxi as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's third year before his reign, after the Wu and Chu Seven Kingdoms rebellion was crushed.

units.zh: 端為人賊戾，又陰痿，一近婦人，病之數月。
units.en: Duan was cruel and violent by temperament, and he also suffered from a hidden affliction of impotence. Whenever he lay with a woman, he would fall ill for months afterward.
units.literal: Duan was cruel and tyrannical by nature, and moreover suffered from impotence. Whenever he approached a woman, he would fall ill for several months.

units.zh: 而有愛幸少年為郎。
units.en: Instead, he kept a favored young man as a gentleman-in-attendance at court.
units.literal: He had a beloved young man who served as a gentleman-in-attendance.

units.zh: 為郎者頃之與後宮亂，端禽滅之，及殺其子母。
units.en: Before long, this attendant carried on illicit affairs with the women of the inner palace. Duan seized and put him to death, and killed his mother and children as well.
units.literal: This attendant soon committed adultery with the women of the rear palace. Duan captured and executed him, along with his mother and children.

units.zh: 數犯上法，漢公卿數請誅端，天子為兄弟之故不忍，而端所為滋甚。
units.en: He transgressed the imperial statutes time and again. The ministers and nobles of the Han court repeatedly petitioned for his execution, but the Son of Heaven, for the bond of brotherhood, could not bring himself to act. Meanwhile, Duan's outrages only grew worse.
units.literal: He repeatedly violated the laws of the court. Han's nobles and ministers repeatedly requested his execution, but the emperor spared him for the sake of brotherhood. Yet Duan's offenses grew worse.

units.zh: 有司再請削其國，去太半。
units.en: The responsible officials twice petitioned to have his kingdom reduced, and more than half its territory was stripped away.
units.literal: The officials twice requested that his kingdom be reduced, removing more than half.

units.zh: 端心慍，遂為無訾省。
units.en: Duan seethed with resentment, and from that point on he spent nothing at all, living in the most extreme frugality.
units.literal: Duan was resentful and became extremely frugal.

units.zh: 府庫壞漏盡，腐財物以巨萬計，終不得收徙。
units.en: His storehouses and treasuries fell into ruin, their roofs leaking, until goods worth tens of millions had rotted away, yet he still refused to collect or relocate them.
units.literal: His storehouses and treasuries all rotted and leaked, with spoiled goods worth millions. In the end he could not collect or move them.

units.zh: 令吏毋得收租賦。
units.en: He forbade his officials from collecting rents or taxes.
units.literal: He ordered his officials not to collect rents and taxes.

units.zh: 端皆去衛，封其宮門，從一門出游。
units.en: Duan dismissed all his guards and sealed every gate of the palace, leaving only a single gate through which he would come and go.
units.literal: Duan dismissed all his guards and sealed his palace gates, going out to travel through only one gate.

units.zh: 數變名姓，為布衣，之他郡國。
units.en: He would frequently change his name, disguise himself as a commoner, and travel incognito to other commanderies and kingdoms.
units.literal: He frequently changed his name and surname, dressed as a commoner, and traveled to other commanderies and kingdoms.

units.zh: 相、二千石往者，奉漢法以治，端輒求其罪告之，無罪者詐藥殺之。
units.en: Whenever a chancellor or an official of two-thousand-shi rank was sent to administer the kingdom, faithfully upholding Han law, Duan would ferret out their transgressions and denounce them. Those against whom he could find no fault, he simply poisoned.
units.literal: When prime ministers and officials of two thousand shi came to serve, they followed Han law to govern. Duan would seek out their crimes and report them. If they were innocent, he would poison them to death.

units.zh: 所以設詐究變，彊足以距諫，智足以飾非。
units.en: He was masterful in devising stratagems and manipulating circumstances, forceful enough to rebuff any remonstrance, and cunning enough to disguise his every transgression.
units.literal: He was skilled at deception and investigation, strong enough to resist remonstrance, and clever enough to disguise his faults.

units.zh: 相、二千石從王治，則漢繩以法。
units.en: If the chancellor or officials of two-thousand-shi rank complied with the king's wishes in governing, then the Han court would hold them accountable under the law.
units.literal: If prime ministers and officials of two thousand shi followed the king's governance, Han would bind them with law.

units.zh: 故膠西小國，而所殺傷二千石甚眾。
units.en: Thus, although Jiaoxi was but a small kingdom, the number of officials of two-thousand-shi rank who were killed or ruined there was remarkably high.
units.literal: Therefore, Jiaoxi was a small kingdom, yet those killed and injured among the two thousand shi officials were very numerous.

units.zh: 立四十七年，卒，竟無男代後，國除，地入于漢，為膠西郡。
units.en: He reigned for forty-seven years and died without ever producing a male heir. His kingdom was abolished, its territory absorbed into the Han domain and reorganized as the Commandery of Jiaoxi.
units.literal: He reigned for forty-seven years and died. In the end he had no male heir to succeed him. The kingdom was abolished and its territory incorporated into Han as Jiaoxi Commandery.

units.zh: 右三國本王皆程姬之子也。
units.en: The founding kings of the above three kingdoms were all sons of Consort Cheng.
units.literal: These three kingdoms were originally ruled by sons of Consort Cheng.

units.zh: 趙王彭祖，以孝景前二年用皇子為廣川王。
units.en: King Pengzu of Zhao was first enfeoffed as King of Guangchuan as an imperial prince in the second year of Emperor Jing's early reign.
units.literal: King Pengzu of Zhao was made King of Guangchuan as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's second year before his reign.

units.zh: 趙王遂反破後，彭祖王廣川。
units.en: After King Sui of Zhao's rebellion was crushed, Pengzu ruled as King of Guangchuan.
units.literal: After King Sui of Zhao's rebellion was crushed, Pengzu became King of Guangchuan.

units.zh: 四年，徙為趙王。
units.en: Four years later, he was transferred to become King of Zhao.
units.literal: After four years, he was moved to become King of Zhao.

units.zh: 十五年，孝景帝崩。
units.en: Fifteen years into his reign, Emperor Jing passed away.
units.literal: After fifteen years, Emperor Xiaojing passed away.

units.zh: 彭祖為人巧佞卑諂，足恭而心刻深。
units.en: Pengzu was by nature artful, fawning, and obsequious, deferential in outward manner but ruthless and calculating at heart.
units.literal: Pengzu was crafty and flattering by nature, outwardly respectful but inwardly deeply treacherous.

units.zh: 好法律，持詭辯以中人。
units.en: He had a passion for legal matters and wielded sophistry to entrap others.
units.literal: He loved legal affairs and used clever arguments to trap people.

units.zh: 彭祖多內寵姬及子孫。
units.en: Pengzu kept a great number of favored consorts in his inner palace, and sired many children and grandchildren.
units.literal: Pengzu had many favored consorts in his palace and many children and grandchildren.

units.zh: 相、二千石欲奉漢法以治，則害於王家。
units.en: Any chancellor or official of two-thousand-shi rank who attempted to govern by Han law inevitably ran afoul of the royal household's interests.
units.literal: If prime ministers and officials of two thousand shi wished to follow Han law to govern, it would harm the king's family.

units.zh: 是以每相、二千石至，彭祖衣皁布衣，自行迎，除二千石舍，多設疑事以作動之，得二千石失言，中忌諱，輒書之。
units.en: For this reason, whenever a new chancellor or official of two-thousand-shi rank arrived, Pengzu would don coarse black cloth and personally go out to welcome him. He would prepare the official's quarters and contrive all manner of provocations to unsettle him. If the official let slip an indiscreet word or violated some taboo, Pengzu recorded it at once.
units.literal: Therefore, whenever prime ministers and officials of two thousand shi arrived, Pengzu would wear mourning clothes and personally go to welcome them. He would clear out the officials' residences and set up many suspicious matters to provoke them. If he caught them making slips of the tongue or taboo violations, he would record them.

units.zh: 二千石欲治者，則以此迫劫；
units.en: Should an official of two-thousand-shi rank attempt to govern, Pengzu would use these records to coerce and threaten him;
units.literal: When officials of two thousand shi wished to govern, he would use this to coerce and threaten them.

units.zh: 不聽，乃上書告，及汙以姦利事。
units.en: and if the official still refused to comply, Pengzu would submit a memorial of accusation to the throne, smearing him with charges of corruption and profiteering.
units.literal: If they did not listen, he would submit memorials accusing them and slander them with charges of corruption and personal gain.

units.zh: 彭祖立五十餘年，相、二千石無能滿二歲，輒以罪去，大者死，小者刑，以故二千石莫敢治。
units.en: Over the course of Pengzu's reign of more than fifty years, not a single chancellor or official of two-thousand-shi rank lasted a full two years before being removed on charges. Those convicted of greater offenses died; those of lesser ones were punished. As a result, no official dared to govern.
units.literal: Pengzu reigned for more than fifty years. No prime minister or official of two thousand shi could complete two years in office before being dismissed for crimes—major ones died, minor ones were punished. Therefore, no officials of two thousand shi dared to govern.

units.zh: 而趙王擅權，使使即縣為賈人榷會，入多於國經租稅。
units.en: The King of Zhao thus monopolized all authority, dispatching agents to the counties to operate trading monopolies on his behalf, which brought in revenue exceeding the kingdom's regular rents and taxes.
units.literal: The King of Zhao monopolized power, sending envoys to counties to act as merchants and collect monopolies, bringing in more than the kingdom's regular taxes.

units.zh: 以是趙王家多金錢，然所賜姬諸子，亦盡之矣。
units.en: As a result, the house of Zhao amassed a great fortune in gold and coin, yet what Pengzu lavished upon his consorts and sons consumed it all.
units.literal: Because of this the Zhao royal family had abundant gold and money, though what he bestowed on his consorts and sons also exhausted it all.

units.zh: 彭祖取笔江都易王寵姬王建所盜與姦淖姬者為姬，甚愛之。
units.en: Pengzu took as his own consort the very Lady Nao whom King Jian of Jiangdu had abducted from the late King Yi's inner palace and bedded unlawfully. Pengzu doted on her greatly.
units.literal: Pengzu took the favored consort of King Yi of Jiangdu that King Jian had stolen and committed adultery with—Nao Ji—as his own consort, and loved her deeply.

units.zh: 彭祖不好治宮室、禨祥，好為吏事。
units.en: Pengzu took no interest in building palaces or pursuing auspicious omens; his passion lay in the business of governance.
units.literal: Pengzu did not like constructing palaces and seeking auspicious omens; he liked handling official matters.

units.zh: 上書願督國中盜賊。
units.en: He petitioned the throne for permission to personally oversee the suppression of bandits and thieves within his kingdom.
units.literal: He submitted a memorial volunteering to supervise thieves and bandits throughout the kingdom.

units.zh: 常夜從走卒行徼邯鄲中。
units.en: He frequently went out at night with foot soldiers on patrol through the streets of Handan.
units.literal: He often went out at night with foot soldiers patrolling Handan.

units.zh: 諸使過客以彭祖險陂，莫敢留邯鄲。
units.en: Envoys and travelers who passed through all regarded Pengzu as dangerous and unpredictable, and none dared linger in Handan.
units.literal: All envoys and travelers passing through considered Pengzu dangerous and treacherous, and none dared stay in Handan.

units.zh: 其太子丹與其女及同產姊姦，與其客江充有卻。
units.en: His crown prince Dan committed incest with his own daughter and with a sister born of the same mother, and fell into a bitter feud with a retainer named Jiang Chong.
units.literal: His crown prince Dan committed incest with his own daughter and full sister, and had enmity with his guest Jiang Chong.

units.zh: 充告丹，丹以故廢。
units.en: Jiang Chong reported Dan's offenses, and as a result Dan was deposed as heir.
units.literal: Chong reported Dan, who was therefore deposed.

units.zh: 趙更立太子。
units.en: The kingdom of Zhao then established a new heir apparent.
units.literal: Zhao established a new crown prince.

units.zh: 中山靖王勝，以孝景前三年用皇子為中山王。
units.en: King Jing of Zhongshan, whose name was Sheng, was enfeoffed as King of Zhongshan as an imperial prince in the third year of Emperor Jing's early reign.
units.literal: King Jing of Zhongshan, Sheng, was made King of Zhongshan as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's third year before his reign.

units.zh: 十四年，孝景帝崩。
units.en: Fourteen years into his reign, Emperor Jing passed away.
units.literal: After fourteen years, Emperor Xiaojing passed away.

units.zh: 勝為人樂酒好內，有子枝屬百二十餘人。
units.en: Sheng was a man who delighted in wine and women, and he fathered more than a hundred and twenty sons and descendants across his branches.
units.literal: Sheng loved wine and women by nature, with over one hundred twenty children and descendants.

units.zh: 常與兄趙王相非，曰：「兄為王，專代吏治事。
units.en: He often quarreled with his elder brother, the King of Zhao, saying: "My brother, though a king, concerns himself solely with taking over the work of officials.
units.literal: He often quarreled with his elder brother, the King of Zhao, saying, "My brother, though a king, monopolizes the work of officials in governing.

units.zh: 王者當日聽音樂聲色。」
units.en: A king ought to spend his days enjoying music and the pleasures of the senses."
units.literal: As king, one should daily listen to music and enjoy beauty.'

units.zh: 趙王亦非之，曰：「中山王徒日淫，不佐天子拊循百姓，何以稱為藩臣！」
units.en: The King of Zhao countered: "The King of Zhongshan does nothing but wallow in excess day after day. He does not assist the Son of Heaven in nurturing and guiding the people. How can he claim to be a worthy vassal?"
units.literal: The King of Zhao also quarreled with him, saying: 'The King of Zhongshan merely indulges in debauchery daily, does not assist the Son of Heaven in comforting and guiding the people. How can he be called a vassal minister!'

units.zh: 立四十二年卒，子哀王昌立。
units.en: After forty-two years on the throne he died, and his son, King Ai, whose name was Chang, succeeded him.
units.literal: He reigned for forty-two years and died. His son, King Ai Chang, succeeded him.

units.zh: 一年卒，子昆侈代為中山王。
units.en: He died after just one year, and his son Kunchi succeeded him as King of Zhongshan.
units.literal: He died after one year. His son Kun Chi succeeded as King of Zhongshan.

units.zh: 右二國本王皆賈夫人之子也。
units.en: The founding kings of the above two kingdoms were both sons of Lady Jia.
units.literal: These two kingdoms were originally ruled by sons of Lady Jia.

units.zh: 長沙定王發，發之母唐姬，故程姬侍者。
units.en: King Ding of Changsha, whose name was Fa, was the son of Consort Tang, who had formerly served as a lady-in-waiting to Consort Cheng.
units.literal: King Ding of Changsha, Fa, Fa's mother Consort Tang, formerly Consort Cheng's attendant.

units.zh: 景帝召程姬，程姬有所辟，不願進，而飾侍者唐兒使夜進。
units.en: When Emperor Jing summoned Consort Cheng, she was indisposed and unwilling to attend. Instead, she adorned her attendant, known as Tang Er, and sent the girl in her place under cover of night.
units.literal: Emperor Jing summoned Consort Cheng. Consort Cheng made some excuse and did not wish to come forward. Instead she dressed up her attendant Tang Er and sent her in at night.

units.zh: 上醉不知，以為程姬而幸之，遂有身。
units.en: The emperor, drunk and unsuspecting, took her for Consort Cheng and lay with her. She conceived.
units.literal: The emperor was drunk and did not realize, thinking it was Consort Cheng and favored her, so she became pregnant.

units.zh: 已乃覺非程姬也。
units.en: Only afterward did the emperor realize that the woman had not been Consort Cheng.
units.literal: Only then did he realize it was not Consort Cheng.

units.zh: 及生子，因命曰發。
units.en: When she gave birth to a son, he was given the name Fa.
units.literal: When she gave birth to a son, he named him Fa.

units.zh: 以孝景前二年用皇子為長沙王。
units.en: In the second year of Emperor Jing's early reign, Fa was enfeoffed as King of Changsha as an imperial prince.
units.literal: In Emperor Xiaojing's second year before his reign, Fa was made King of Changsha as imperial son.

units.zh: 以其母微，無寵，故王卑溼貧國。
units.en: Because his mother was of humble origin and enjoyed no imperial favor, he was consigned to rule over a poor and swampy kingdom.
units.literal: Because his mother was of lowly status and had no favor, he was made king of a poor and damp kingdom.

units.zh: 立二十七年卒，子康王庸立。
units.en: After twenty-seven years on the throne he died, and his son, King Kang, whose name was Yong, succeeded him.
units.literal: He reigned for twenty-seven years and died. His son, King Kang Yong, succeeded him.

units.zh: 二十八年，卒，子鮒鮈立為長沙王。
units.en: He died after twenty-eight years, and his son Fugui succeeded him as King of Changsha.
units.literal: He died after twenty-eight years. His son Fu You succeeded as King of Changsha.

units.zh: 右一國本王唐姬之子也。
units.en: The founding king of the above kingdom was a son of Consort Tang.
units.literal: This one kingdom was originally ruled by a son of Consort Tang.

units.zh: 廣川惠王越，以孝景中二年用皇子為廣川王。
units.en: King Hui of Guangchuan, whose name was Yue, was enfeoffed as King of Guangchuan as an imperial prince in the second year of Emperor Jing's middle reign.
units.literal: King Hui of Guangchuan, Yue, was made King of Guangchuan as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's middle second year.

units.zh: 十二年卒，子齊立為王。
units.en: After twelve years he died, and his son Qi was established as king.
units.literal: He died after twelve years. His son Qi succeeded as king.

units.zh: 齊有幸臣桑距。
units.en: Qi had a favored retainer named Sang Ju.
units.literal: Qi had a favored minister named Sang Ju.

units.zh: 已而有罪，欲誅距，距亡，王因禽其宗族。
units.en: In time Sang Ju committed an offense. The king sought to have him executed, but Ju fled. The king then seized Ju's entire clan.
units.literal: Later Sang Ju committed a crime. Qi wished to execute him, but Ju fled. The king then captured Ju's clan.

units.zh: 距怨王，乃上書告王齊與同產姦。
units.en: Harboring bitter resentment, Ju submitted a memorial to the throne accusing King Qi of incest with his own sister.
units.literal: Ju resented the king and submitted a memorial accusing King Qi of committing incest with his full sister.

units.zh: 自是之後，王齊數上書告言漢公卿及幸臣所忠等。
units.en: From that time on, King Qi repeatedly submitted memorials denouncing Han ministers and nobles, as well as imperial favorites such as Suo Zhong and others.
units.literal: From then on, King Qi repeatedly submitted memorials accusing Han's nobles and ministers as well as favored officials like Suo Zhong and others.

units.zh: 膠東康王寄，以孝景中二年用皇子為膠東王。
units.en: King Kang of Jiaodong, whose name was Ji, was enfeoffed as King of Jiaodong as an imperial prince in the second year of Emperor Jing's middle reign.
units.literal: King Kang of Jiaodong, Ji, was made King of Jiaodong as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's middle second year.

units.zh: 二十八年卒。
units.en: He died after twenty-eight years on the throne.
units.literal: He died after twenty-eight years.

units.zh: 淮南王謀反時，寄微聞其事，私作樓車鏃矢戰守備，候淮南之起。
units.en: When the King of Huainan was plotting rebellion, Ji caught wind of the scheme and secretly had siege towers, arrowheads, and other military defenses constructed, standing ready for the moment Huainan would rise.
units.literal: During the Huainan king's rebellion, Ji had heard rumors of the matter. He privately built tower chariots, arrowheads, and defensive preparations, waiting for Huainan's uprising.

units.zh: 及吏治淮南之事，辭出之。
units.en: When officials investigated the Huainan affair, the confessions that emerged implicated him.
units.literal: When officials investigated the Huainan affair, the evidence implicated him.

units.zh: 寄於上最親，意傷之，發病而死，不敢置後，於是上（問）［聞］。
units.en: Ji had been the emperor's most beloved brother, and the affair weighed heavily upon him. He fell ill with grief and died, not having dared to designate an heir. Only then did the emperor learn what had happened.
units.literal: Ji was most beloved by the emperor, who was grieved by this. Ji fell ill and died, not daring to appoint an heir. Thus, the emperor heard of it.

units.zh: 寄有長子者名賢，母無寵；
units.en: Ji's eldest son was named Xian, but his mother had never enjoyed imperial favor;
units.literal: Ji had an eldest son named Xian whose mother had no favor.

units.zh: 少子名慶，母愛幸，寄常欲立之，為不次，因有過，遂無言。
units.en: his younger son was named Qing, whose mother was beloved and favored. Ji had always wished to name Qing as his heir, but since doing so would violate the order of succession, and because of the taint of his own offenses, he said nothing.
units.literal: His younger son was named Qing, whose mother was beloved and favored. Ji had often wished to establish Qing as heir, but since it would violate proper order, and because he himself had offenses, he said nothing.

units.zh: 上憐之，乃以賢為膠東王奉康王嗣，而封慶於故衡山地，為六安王。
units.en: The emperor, moved by pity, made Xian King of Jiaodong to carry on King Kang's line, and enfeoffed Qing in the former territory of Hengshan as King of Liu'an.
units.literal: The emperor pitied him and made Xian King of Jiaodong to continue King Kang's line, while enfeoffing Qing in the former Hengshan territory as King of Liu'an.

units.zh: 膠東王賢立十四年卒，謚為哀王。
units.en: King Xian of Jiaodong reigned for fourteen years and died. He was posthumously titled King Ai.
units.literal: King Xian of Jiaodong reigned for fourteen years and died. His posthumous title was King Ai.

units.zh: 子慶為王。
units.en: His son Qing succeeded him as king.
units.literal: His son Qing became king.

units.zh: 六安王慶，以元狩二年用膠東康王子為六安王。
units.en: King Qing of Liu'an, a son of King Kang of Jiaodong, was enfeoffed as King of Liu'an in the second year of the Yuanshou era.
units.literal: King Qing of Liu'an was made King of Liu'an as son of King Kang of Jiaodong in the second year of Yuanshou.

units.zh: 清河哀王乘，以孝景中三年用皇子為清河王。
units.en: King Ai of Qinghe, whose name was Cheng, was enfeoffed as King of Qinghe as an imperial prince in the third year of Emperor Jing's middle reign.
units.literal: King Ai of Qinghe, Cheng, was made King of Qinghe as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's middle third year.

units.zh: 十二年卒，無後，國除，地入于漢，為清河郡。
units.en: He died after twelve years without an heir. His kingdom was abolished, its territory absorbed into the Han domain and reorganized as the Commandery of Qinghe.
units.literal: He died after twelve years with no heirs. The kingdom was abolished and its territory incorporated into Han as Qinghe Commandery.

units.zh: 常山憲王舜，以孝景中五年用皇子為常山王。
units.en: King Xian of Changshan, whose name was Shun, was enfeoffed as King of Changshan as an imperial prince in the fifth year of Emperor Jing's middle reign.
units.literal: King Xian of Changshan, Shun, was made King of Changshan as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's middle fifth year.

units.zh: 舜最親，景帝少子，驕怠多淫，數犯禁，上常寬釋之。
units.en: Shun was the most cherished of the brothers, being Emperor Jing's youngest son. He was arrogant, indolent, and given to excess, and he frequently ran afoul of the law. Yet the emperor always pardoned him.
units.literal: Shun was most beloved. As Emperor Jing's youngest son, he was arrogant and indolent, frequently committing excesses. The emperor often pardoned him leniently.

units.zh: 立三十二年卒，太子勃代立為王。
units.en: After thirty-two years on the throne he died, and his heir apparent, Bo, succeeded him as king.
units.literal: He reigned for thirty-two years and died. Crown Prince Bo succeeded as king.

units.zh: 初，憲王舜有所不愛姬生長男棁。
units.en: Originally, King Xian Shun had a consort whom he did not favor, and she bore him his eldest son, Tiao.
units.literal: At first, King Xian Shun had an unfavored consort who bore his eldest son Tiao.

units.zh: 棁以母無寵故，亦不得幸於王。
units.en: Because his mother enjoyed no favor, Tiao likewise received none from the king.
units.literal: Because his mother had no favor, Tiao also did not receive favor from the king.

units.zh: 王後修生太子勃。
units.en: The queen, whose name was Xiu, later bore the crown prince, Bo.
units.literal: Later the queen bore Crown Prince Bo.

units.zh: 王內多，所幸姬生子平、子商，王后希得幸。
units.en: The king kept many women in his inner palace, and his favored consorts bore him sons named Ping and Shang. The queen herself rarely enjoyed his attentions.
units.literal: The king had many consorts. His favored consorts bore sons Ping and Shang. The queen rarely received favor.

units.zh: 及憲王病甚，諸幸姬常侍病，故王后亦以妒媢不常侍病，輒歸舍。
units.en: When King Xian fell gravely ill, his favored consorts took turns attending at his bedside. The queen, out of jealous resentment, declined to attend regularly and would withdraw to her own chambers.
units.literal: When King Xian fell gravely ill, his favored consorts constantly attended to his illness. The queen, out of jealousy, did not constantly attend but would return to her chambers.

units.zh: 醫進藥，太子勃不自嘗藥，又不宿留侍病。
units.en: When the physician prepared medicine, Crown Prince Bo did not taste it first to test it, as filial duty required, nor did he keep vigil at his father's bedside through the night.
units.literal: When the physician administered medicine, Crown Prince Bo did not personally taste the medicine, nor did he stay overnight attending to the illness.

units.zh: 及王薨，王后、太子乃至。
units.en: Only when the king breathed his last did the queen and the crown prince finally appear.
units.literal: Only when the king passed away did the queen and crown prince arrive.

units.zh: 憲王雅不以長子棁為人數，及薨，又不分與財物。
units.en: King Xian had never treated his eldest son Tiao as a person of consequence, and upon his death he left Tiao no share of the estate.
units.literal: King Xian had never considered his eldest son Tiao as part of the family. When he died, he did not divide any property with him.

units.zh: 郎或說太子、王后，令諸子與長子棁共分財物，太子、王后不聽。
units.en: Certain gentlemen-attendants urged the crown prince and queen to let the other sons share the estate with the eldest, Tiao, but neither would hear of it.
units.literal: Some gentlemen advised the crown prince and queen to have the various sons share property with the eldest son Tiao. The crown prince and queen did not listen.

units.zh: 太子代立，又不收恤棁。
units.en: Even after the crown prince succeeded to the throne, he still refused to look after Tiao or offer him any support.
units.literal: After succeeding the throne, he still neglected Tiao.

units.zh: 棁怨王后、太子。
units.en: Tiao nursed a deep grudge against the queen and the crown prince.
units.literal: Tiao resented the queen and crown prince.

units.zh: 漢使者視憲王喪，棁自言憲王病時，王后、太子不侍，及薨，六日出舍，太子勃私姦，飲酒，博戲，擊筑，與女子載馳，環城過市，入牢視囚。
units.en: When Han envoys arrived to oversee King Xian's funeral, Tiao came forward and personally testified that during the king's illness, neither the queen nor the crown prince had attended him. After the king's death, they had left their mourning quarters within six days. He further reported that Crown Prince Bo had conducted illicit affairs, drunk wine, gambled, and played the bamboo zither. He had raced in carriages with women through the streets, ridden around the city walls and through the markets, and entered the prison to inspect the inmates.
units.literal: Han envoys inspecting King Xian's funeral, Tiao personally stated that during King Xian's illness, the queen and crown prince did not attend. When he died, they left the residence after six days. Crown Prince Bo privately committed adultery, drank wine, gambled, played zither, raced chariots with women, circled the city through the markets, and entered prisons to inspect prisoners.

units.zh: 天子遣大行騫驗王后及問王勃，請逮勃所與姦諸證左，王又匿之。
units.en: The Son of Heaven dispatched the Grand Herald, Qian, to investigate the queen and interrogate King Bo. He requested the arrest of all accomplices and witnesses to Bo's illicit activities, but the king concealed them.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven sent Grand Herald Qian to investigate the queen and interrogate King Bo, requesting to arrest Bo's accomplices in adultery and witnesses. The king hid them.

units.zh: 吏求捕勃大急，使人致擊笞掠，擅出漢所疑囚者。
units.en: When the officials pressed urgently to apprehend Bo, he had his men resort to beatings and floggings, and he took it upon himself to release prisoners whom the Han court had placed under suspicion.
units.literal: When officials urgently sought to apprehend Bo, he had men inflict beatings and floggings, and arbitrarily released prisoners whom the Han court held under suspicion.

units.zh: 有司請誅憲王後修及王勃。
units.en: The responsible officials petitioned to have Queen Xiu and King Bo put to death.
units.literal: The officials requested execution of King Xian's queen Xiu and King Bo.

units.zh: 上以修素無行，使棁陷之罪，勃無良師傅，不忍誅。
units.en: The emperor, reflecting that Xiu had always been of poor conduct, making it easy for Tiao to entrap her, and that Bo had never had the benefit of a worthy tutor, could not bring himself to have them executed.
units.literal: The emperor, considering that Xiu had always been immoral, allowing Tiao to frame her with crimes, and Bo had no good teachers, could not bear to execute them.

units.zh: 有司請廢王後修，徙王勃以家屬處房陵，上許之。
units.en: The officials petitioned instead to depose Queen Xiu and exile King Bo along with his family to Fangling. The emperor consented.
units.literal: The officials requested deposing Queen Xiu and exiling King Bo with his family to Fangling. The emperor approved.

units.zh: 勃王數月，遷于房陵，國絕。
units.en: Bo had reigned as king for only a few months before he was removed to Fangling, and the kingdom came to an end.
units.literal: Bo had been king for several months when he was moved to Fangling. The kingdom was extinguished.

units.zh: 月餘，天子為最親，乃詔有司曰：「常山憲王蚤夭，后妾不和，適孽誣爭，陷于不義以滅國，朕甚閔焉。
units.en: A little more than a month later, mindful that Changshan had been ruled by his closest kin, the Son of Heaven issued an edict to his ministers: "King Xian of Changshan died before his time. His queen and consorts were at odds, and legitimate and illegitimate sons slandered one another and quarreled until they fell into disgrace and the kingdom was extinguished. We are deeply grieved by this.
units.literal: More than a month later, considering that he was most beloved, the emperor instructed the officials: 'King Xian of Changshan died young. His queen and consorts were not harmonious. Legitimate and illegitimate sons slandered and contended, falling into unrighteousness and extinguishing the kingdom. I greatly pity this.

units.zh: 其封憲王子平三萬戶，為真定王；
units.en: Enfeoff King Xian's son Ping as King of Zhending, with thirty thousand households;
units.literal: Let King Xian's son Ping be enfeoffed with thirty thousand households as King of Zhending;

units.zh: 封子商三萬戶，為泗水王。」
units.en: and enfeoff his son Shang as King of Sishui, also with thirty thousand households."
units.literal: and let his son Shang be enfeoffed with thirty thousand households as King of Sishui."

units.zh: 真定王平，元鼎四年用常山憲王子為真定王。
units.en: King Ping of Zhending, a son of King Xian of Changshan, was enfeoffed as King of Zhending in the fourth year of the Yuanding era.
units.literal: King Ping of Zhending was made King of Zhending as son of King Xian of Changshan in the fourth year of Yuanding.

units.zh: 泗水思王商，以元鼎四年用常山憲王子為泗水王。
units.en: King Si of Sishui, whose name was Shang, a son of King Xian of Changshan, was enfeoffed as King of Sishui in the fourth year of the Yuanding era.
units.literal: King Si of Sishui, Shang, was made King of Sishui as son of King Xian of Changshan in the fourth year of Yuanding.

units.zh: 十一年卒，子哀王安世立。
units.en: After eleven years he died, and his son, King Ai, whose name was Anshi, succeeded him.
units.literal: He died after eleven years. His son, King Ai Anshi, succeeded him.

units.zh: 十一年卒，無子。
units.en: He died after eleven years without a son.
units.literal: He died after eleven years with no sons.

units.zh: 於是上憐泗水王絕，乃立安世弟賀為泗水王。
units.en: The emperor, grieved that the Sishui line had come to an end, established Anshi's younger brother He as King of Sishui.
units.literal: The emperor pitied the extinction of the Sishui line and established Anshi's younger brother He as King of Sishui.

units.zh: 右四國本王皆王夫人兒姁子也。
units.en: The founding kings of the above four kingdoms were all sons of Lady Wang, also known as Erxu.
units.literal: The founding kings of the above four kingdoms were all sons of Lady Wang Erxu.

units.zh: 其後漢益封其支子為六安王、泗水王二國。
units.en: In later years, the Han court further enfeoffed their collateral descendants, creating two additional kingdoms: Liu'an and Sishui.
units.literal: Later Han further enfeoffed their branch descendants as kings of Liu'an and Sishui, two kingdoms.

units.zh: 凡兒姁子孫，於今為六王。
units.en: In all, the descendants of Erxu now hold six royal titles.
units.literal: In all, Erxu's descendants now number six kings.

units.zh: 太史公曰：高祖時諸侯皆賦，得自除內史以下，漢獨為置丞相，黃金印。
units.en: The Grand Historian remarks: In the time of Emperor Gaozu, the feudal lords all collected their own taxes and were permitted to appoint their own officials from the rank of Interior Minister downward. Only the chancellors were appointed by the Han court, and they bore golden seals.
units.literal: The Grand Historian says: In Gaozu's time the feudal lords all collected their own taxes and were able to appoint their own officials from the rank of interior minister downward. Only the Han court appointed chancellors for them, with golden seals.

units.zh: 諸侯自除御史、廷尉正、博士，擬於天子。
units.en: The feudal lords appointed their own censors, chief justices, and erudites, rivaling the Son of Heaven in their establishments.
units.literal: The feudal lords appointed their own censors, directors of convicts at the Court of Justice, and erudites, rivaling the Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 自吳楚反後，五宗王世，漢為置二千石，去「丞相」曰「相」，銀印。
units.en: After the rebellion of Wu and Chu, through the successive generations of the five royal lineages, the Han court appointed officials of two-thousand-shi rank in every kingdom, replaced the title of "chancellor" with the lesser designation of "administrator," and issued silver seals in place of gold.
units.literal: After the Wu and Chu rebellion, the five clans of kings generation after generation, Han appointed officials of two thousand shi for them, removed 'chancellor' and called it 'prime minister', silver seal.

units.zh: 諸侯獨得食租稅，奪之權。
units.en: The feudal lords were left with nothing but the right to collect their rents and taxes; all real power had been stripped away.
units.literal: The feudal lords only received rent taxes, their power was taken away.

units.zh: 其後諸侯貧者或乘牛車也。
units.en: In the years that followed, some of the more impoverished feudal lords were even reduced to riding in ox-drawn carts.
units.literal: Afterward the impoverished feudal lords sometimes rode ox-carts.
